short: Sixty-two years on the throne, from military expansion and defeat to a symbolic monarchy.
full:
Hirohito acceded on his father's death in December 1926, having already served five years as regent. His reign is the longest in Japanese history. Its first two decades saw the army seize Manchuria in 1931 without cabinet approval, officers murder ministers in the coup attempts of 1932 and 1936, war with China from 1937, and the alliance with Germany and Italy that led to the Pacific war and, in 1945, to defeat.

How far he directed those events is the central question about him. He was briefed constantly and sanctioned the decisions taken in his name, including the strike at Pearl Harbor; he also intervened directly twice, against the 1936 mutineers and in August 1945 to accept the Potsdam terms, when he broadcast the surrender in a recorded address most Japanese had never heard him give. The occupation kept him on the throne and did not indict him. He renounced his divinity in 1946, became a constitutional symbol in 1947, took up marine biology, and reigned through the post-war economic boom until his death on 7 January 1989.
